app_text: HC Yellow 11 is banned for use as a hair dye substance in the EU under Annex II/1236 of EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009.
HC Orange 3 is banned for use as a hair dye substance in the EU under Annex II/1237 of EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009.
HC Green 1 is banned for use as a hair dye substance in the EU under Annex II/1238 of EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009.
HC Red 8 is banned for use as a hair dye substance in the EU under Annex II/1239 of EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009.
Disperse Red 15 is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/1241, except as an impurity in Disperse Violet 1.
Phytonadione (Vitamin K1) is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/1371. It is a pharmaceutical substance that is not permitted in cosmetics.
Benzylparaben is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/1377. Unlike some other parabens, benzylparaben has no permitted uses in EU cosmetics.
Pentylparaben is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/1378. It is a paraben preservative with endocrine disrupting properties.
Atranol is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/1381. It is a potent skin sensitiser and allergen naturally found in oakmoss and treemoss.
Chloroatranol is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/1382. It is an extremely potent skin sensitiser and allergen naturally found in oakmoss and treemoss.

Formaldehyde itself is banned as a cosmetic ingredient in the EU under Annex II/1577. It is a known carcinogen and skin sensitiser. Important note: Some preservatives that slowly release formaldehyde (such as DMDM Hydantoin, Imidazolidinyl Urea, Quaternium-15, Diazolidinyl Urea) are separately regulated under Annex V and are permitted at low concentrations — these are different from formaldehyde itself being listed as an ingredient.
restriction_details: Banned as a direct ingredient. Formaldehyde-releasing preservatives are separately regulated under Annex V with concentration limits.

app_text: Paraformaldehyde is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/1578. It releases formaldehyde and shares its carcinogenic and sensitising properties.

alternative_names: PFOA, C8, Heptadecafluorooctanoic acid, Ammonium pentadecafluorooctanoate
classification: PFAS, Persistent organic pollutant, Reprotoxin, Carcinogen
app_text: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) is a PFAS (forever chemical) banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/1561. PFOA is persistent in the environment and human body, and is classified as carcinogenic and reprotoxic.

Perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS) is a PFAS (forever chemical) banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/1493. PFOS is one of the most persistent environmental pollutants and is associated with reproductive and developmental toxicity.

Bisphenol A (BPA) is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/1176. BPA is a well-known endocrine disruptor that can interfere with hormonal systems and has particular concerns for reproductive health and fetal development.

Dibutyl Phthalate (DBP) is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/675. It is a reprotoxin and endocrine disruptor that was commonly used as a nail polish plasticiser before being banned.
Diethylhexyl Phthalate (DEHP) is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/677. It is one of the most widely studied endocrine disruptors and reprotoxins.
Benzyl Butyl Phthalate (BBP) is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/1152. It is a reprotoxin and endocrine disruptor particularly relevant for pregnancy safety.
Diisobutyl Phthalate (DIBP) is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/1492. It is classified as a reproductive toxin.
Dicyclohexyl Phthalate (DCHP) is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/1637. It is a reprotoxin and endocrine disruptor.
Dihexyl Phthalate is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/1559. It is classified as a reproductive toxin.

alternative_names: Retinoic acid, All-trans retinoic acid, Vitamin A acid
app_text: Tretinoin (retinoic acid) is banned as a cosmetic ingredient in the EU under Annex II/375. It is one of the most critical ingredients to avoid during pregnancy due to its potent teratogenic effects (can cause serious birth defects). Note: Tretinoin IS legally available as a prescription medicine — if you have been prescribed it, speak to your doctor about pregnancy safety. However it should never appear on a cosmetic product label.
restriction_details: Banned in cosmetics (Annex II). Permitted as a prescription pharmaceutical under separate medicines legislation. Do not use cosmetics containing this ingredient during pregnancy.

app_text: Musk Ambrette is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/414. It is a synthetic musk fragrance banned due to neurotoxicity and photoallergy concerns.

Hexachlorophene is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/371. It was formerly used as an antimicrobial agent but banned due to serious neurotoxicity, particularly in infants, and reproductive toxicity concerns.

Nonylphenol is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/1168. It is a well-documented endocrine disruptor that mimics estrogen and has particular concerns for reproductive health and development.

classification: Persistent organic pollutant, Endocrine Disruptor, Reprotoxin
app_text: Hexabromocyclododecane (HBCD) is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/1546. It is a persistent organic pollutant, endocrine disruptor and reproductive toxin found as a contaminant in some products.
Tris(2-Chloroethyl) Phosphate (TCEP) is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/1004. It is a carcinogen and reproductive toxin formerly used as a flame retardant.

Ketoconazole is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/1528. It is an antifungal drug that is an endocrine disruptor, particularly affecting testosterone production. Especially concerning during pregnancy.
Diethylene Glycol (DEG) is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/1370. It is a nephrotoxin (kidney poison) that has caused fatal poisonings when used in cosmetics and medicines.
Formamide is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/744. It is classified as a reproductive toxin and teratogen.
Pyrocatechol (Catechol) is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/408. It is classified as a carcinogen and mutagen.
Pyrogallol is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/409. It was formerly used as a hair dye chemical but banned due to mutagenicity and reproductive toxicity concerns.
Minoxidil is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/372. It is a pharmaceutical drug (used medically for hair loss) that is not permitted as a cosmetic ingredient.

Urocanic acid is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/418. It was formerly used as a UV filter/sunscreen ingredient but banned due to immunosuppressive effects when exposed to UV light and potential links to melanoma risk. Note: It occurs naturally in human skin but is not permitted as an added cosmetic ingredient.
restriction_details: Banned as a cosmetic ingredient. Occurs naturally in skin but cannot be added to cosmetic products.

app_text: Aristolochic acid is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/365. It is a potent carcinogen and nephrotoxin found in some herbal and botanical ingredients.
Benzidine is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/26. It is a potent carcinogen formerly used in hair dyes.
Cobalt and its compounds are banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/1645. Cobalt is a carcinogen, reproductive toxin and potent skin sensitiser.
Cobalt dichloride is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/453. It is carcinogenic, reprotoxic and a potent skin sensitiser.
Nickel and its compounds are banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/1093. Nickel is one of the most common causes of allergic contact dermatitis and is classified as carcinogenic.

Potassium bromate is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/461. It was formerly used as an oxidising agent in hair perming neutralisers but banned due to its classification as a carcinogen. Note: Some older hair products from outside the EU may still contain it.
restriction_details: Absolute ban in cosmetics. No permitted exceptions.

app_text: Safrole is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/360, except where it occurs naturally in essential oils at normal background concentrations below the permitted threshold. It is a carcinogen and genotoxin. If listed as a named ingredient on a cosmetic label, that product is non-compliant.
restriction_details: Banned in cosmetics except for trace natural content in essential oils below threshold levels.

app_text: Naphthalene is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/1167. It is classified as a carcinogen.
Disperse Yellow 3 is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/1055. It is a hair dye chemical classified as carcinogenic.
Hexachlorobenzene is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/652. It is a persistent organic pollutant, carcinogen and reproductive toxin.
Trichloroethylene is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/645. It is a carcinogen and reproductive toxin.
Acrylamide is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/681 (unless regulated elsewhere). It is a carcinogen, mutagen, neurotoxin and reproductive toxin.

1,4-Dioxane is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/343. It is a carcinogen that does not typically appear on ingredient lists because it is a byproduct contaminant rather than an intentionally added ingredient. It can form during the manufacturing of ethoxylated ingredients (those with "eth" in their name, like Sodium Laureth Sulfate, PEG compounds). Its presence indicates a manufacturing quality issue.
restriction_details: Banned. Typically appears as a manufacturing contaminant in ethoxylated ingredients rather than as a listed ingredient.

app_text: Sodium pyrithione is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/369 due to reproductive toxicity and teratogenicity. Important note: Zinc pyrithione (a different compound) is regulated separately under Annex III and is permitted in anti-dandruff shampoos at concentrations up to 1%. If you see "Pyrithione Zinc" or "Zinc Pyrithione" on a shampoo label, that is the permitted form — not the same as Sodium Pyrithione.
restriction_details: Sodium pyrithione is banned. Zinc pyrithione (different compound) is permitted under Annex III for anti-dandruff use only.

app_text: 4-Benzyloxyphenol (monobenzone) is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/178. It was used as a skin lightening agent but banned due to sensitisation and permanent depigmentation risks.
Chloroform is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/366. It is a carcinogen and reproductive toxin formerly used as a solvent.
2-Naphthol is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/241. It was formerly used in hair dyes but banned due to mutagenicity concerns.
Phenol is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/1175. It is a neurotoxin and reproductive toxin formerly used as a preservative and antiseptic.

Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/338. It is an extremely effective skin penetration enhancer that can carry other chemicals — including harmful ones — through the skin barrier, increasing systemic absorption. Particularly concerning during pregnancy as it could enhance absorption of other potentially harmful ingredients.
restriction_details: Banned in cosmetics. May be used in pharmaceutical/medical products under separate legislation.

app_text: 4-tert-Butylphenol is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/340. It is an endocrine disruptor and can cause chemical leukoderma (depigmentation of skin).
Malononitrile is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/149.
Benzene is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/47. It is a potent carcinogen and mutagen. It can appear as a contaminant in some cosmetic ingredients derived from petroleum.
Carbon disulphide is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/73. It is a neurotoxin and reproductive toxin.
Hexane is banned in cosmetic products in the EU under Annex II/999. It is a neurotoxin and reproductive toxin sometimes used as a solvent in cosmetic manufacturing.
